title: Reliability Debt Retreat - Sprint Canvas and Handoff Plan
content:
Purpose and intent:
This doc is a working sprint canvas for a condensed "debt retreat" focused on removing small-to-medium reliability debt items that are high-impact for SLO attainment. Goal is to create a 3-week cross-functional program to (a) reduce alert noise and false positives, (b) close 8 targeted SLO gaps, and (c) hand off durable ownership changes to product teams with clear runbook updates.

Context and why now:
- Post-Q4 incident review showed repeated noise from batch job throttling and a set of flaky external dependency checks that drive p99 latency breaches.
- Several product teams are moving toward Dedicated deployments; we need to tighten SLO baselines before ramp.
- This is intentionally narrow: short-lived, high ROI tickets with clear owners and rollback paths.

Success criteria (how we know this worked):
- 8 targeted SLO signal gaps moved from Red->Amber/Green within 4 weeks of sprint close.
- Alert noise reduced by >=40% on the SRE oncall roster for the targeted services (measured by alert counts/week).
- 100% of modified runbooks reviewed and merged, with owner assigned in the service manifest.
- At least one automated mitigation (circuit-breaker or adaptive backoff) deployed for external dependency failures.

Scope (in-scope / out-of-scope):
In-scope:
- Services A, B, C (frontline model-serving, prefix cache, and embeddings index)
- SLO review, alert tuning, small infra config changes (timeouts, retries), and runbook edits
- Ownership transfer items and simple automation (feature-flagged)

Out-of-scope:
- Major architectural rewrites or data model migrations
- Long-running capacity purchases or Dedicated re-architecture

Cross-functional roles (fast RACI sketch):
- SRE lead (Asha Patel) — program convener, triage owner, release gating
- Service owners (Marcus Li for Service A, Sofia Chen for Service B, Jordan Rivera for Service C) — implement changes, PRs, runbook edits
- Platform infra (Priya Desai) — kernel/instance tuning, autoscaling rules, capacity shortlists
- Observability (Ethan Park) — dashboards, alert tuning, event tagging for noise measurement
- Solutions / SE (on-call rota) — customer impact validation and deploy acceptance

Top candidate tickets (quick list with short rationale):
- OPS-2312: Reduce noisy 5xx alerts on Service A by collapsing duplicate triggers (rationale: alerts tied to internal health probes firing during short GC spikes). Estimated 2d.
- SRV-1988: Add adaptive retry with jitter to external census API calls (rationale: external rate-limited timeouts cause backpressure leading to p99 spikes). Estimated 3d.
- INFRA-314: Lower default write timeout for cache shard sync + add circuit-breaker for shard eviction (rationale: long sync holds threads, causes queueing). Estimated 3d.
- ENG-xxxx: Consolidate thin-run features in the deployment pipeline that cause spiky restarts for Service B (rationale: repeated restarts show up as momentary latency). Estimated 2d.
- OBS-4001: Consolidate alert policies and add an alert-suppression window tied to deployment events (rationale: rollout churn creates false positives). Estimated 2d.
- DOC-900: Runbook update template and owner assignment for all changes (rationale: prevent knowledge gaps). Estimated 1d.
- QA-777: Add synthetic p99 test probing for the embeddings index (rationale: catch regressions earlier). Estimated 3d.

Sprint structure (3 weeks):
- Week 0 (planning / intake, 3 days): finalize ticket list, confirm owners, schedule daily 30m standups, create measurement dashboards.
- Week 1 (execution): implement fixes for low-risk tickets (OPS-2312, DOC-900, OBS-4001). Feature-flag deployments, monitoring smoke tests.
- Week 2 (execution + validation): deploy INFRA-314 and SRV-1988, run synthetic tests, iterate on timeouts and circuit-breaker thresholds.
- Week 3 (hardening + handoff): merge runbook edits, assign owners in service manifest, post-mortem-lite, update SLA/SLO dashboards, close the loop with product stakeholders.

Daily rituals and communication:
- 30m standup (12:00 PT) — quick progress, blockers, deploy windows
- SRE triage board in Jira updated before EOD each day
- Slack channel #debt-retreat-2026 (pinned checklist & deploy schedule)
- Friday demo + short runbook walkthrough (20m) with product owners

Measurement plan (how we’ll track impact):
- Baseline capture (prior to start): alert counts last 2 weeks, SLO burn rate for target services, p50/p95/p99 latencies, foo_error_rate.
- Week-over-week dashboard showing: alert counts, SLO burn rate, deploy-related alerts, synthetic probe success rate.
- Post-sprint 30-day review to validate signal stability and ensure changes haven’t regressed throughput/cost.

Risk register and mitigations:
- Risk: Fix causes performance regression under heavy load. Mitigation: Feature-flag and canary 1% traffic, automated rollback on error budget breach.
- Risk: Ownership handoff not accepted by product team. Mitigation: Require sign-off during Friday demo and include a 2-week support commitment from SRE.
- Risk: External dependency behavior changes after adaptive retry. Mitigation: Add observability hooks and temporary circuit-breaker with short TTL.

Deployment guardrails:
- No change to SLO window definitions during sprint without exec sign-off.
- All infra changes must include a rollback plan and canary threshold.
- No bulk database schema changes allowed in this program.

Handoff checklist (must be completed before ticket close):
- PR merged for code change and tag in release notes
- Runbook updated with owner, symptoms, mitigation steps, postmortem link if applicable
- Dashboard panel added showing the primary signal and burn rate
- Product owner sign-off in Jira comment
- Oncall play added to the weekly rota for 2 weeks post-change

Open questions / decisions needed:
- Do we permit soft-failures on synthetic probes for 48 hours as we tune thresholds? (TBD — SRE to propose)
- Is the Solutions team comfortable owning the new circuit-breaker behavior if it impacts API semantics? (Sofia to confirm)
- Do we tag these changes as a "reliability opt-in" in the release notes for customer transparency? (Legal/PR guidance if yes)

Appendix: quick links and notes
- Baseline dashboard: CONFLUENCE:REL-452-retro-capture (see section "metrics snapshot")
- Key PRs to watch: github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/314, github.com/services/service-a/pull/1988
- Slack/meeting: Booked "Friday demo" calendar with product leads (cal invite: "Debt Retreat - Demo")

Quick wins (low friction, high impact list):
- Remove duplicate alert policy for health_probe_5xx (15–30m)
- Shorten cache shard sync timeout from 20s->3s behind a circuit-breaker (1–2d)
- Add a synthetic p99 probe for embeddings index (2–3d)
notes: Working doc — intentionally terse in places; expect follow-ups and ticket churn. Prioritize fixes that have automated rollback paths and quantifiable telemetry.
